canonical_statement: For every natural number n at least 3 and every smooth compactly supported real-valued function u on Euclidean R^n, the integral of |u(x)|^2 / ||x||^2 is at most (2/(n-2))^2 times the integral of the squared norm of the Frechet derivative of u.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat; u : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n) -> Real; proposition in Prop
conclusion: integral x, |u x|^2 / ||x||^2 <= (2 / ((n : Real) - 2))^2 * integral x, ||fderiv Real u x||^2
minimal_import_check: Deleting each listed direct import separately makes Statement.lean fail to elaborate; two initially tested imports were removed as redundant.
statement_selection: This is the exact Euclidean differential L2 variant frozen by intake. It does not substitute a discrete, one-dimensional, fractional, boundary-domain, or Rellich inequality.
degenerate_cases: Dimensions 0, 1, and 2 are excluded. Lean's totalized real division gives the singular integrand value zero at x = 0; this differs only on the volume-null singleton in positive dimension. The zero function is included.

killed: dimension lower bound changed from 3 to 2
